h1:
Phang Nga Cafes
Takua Pa Old Town + Khao Lak Beachside
intro: Phang Nga has two very different cafe scenes. In Takua Pa Old Town you're sitting inside 100-year-old Sino-Portuguese shophouses, nursing a coffee while the afternoon light hits the worn tiles. Over in Khao Lak it's beachfront spots with Andaman Sea breezes and sunset views. We picked 10 places that locals actually go to — with neighborhoods, opening hours, and rough price ranges so you can plan properly.

blocks.html: If you think Phang Nga is only beaches and islands, the cafes here will change your mind. Takua Pa Old Town has a row of Sino-Portuguese shophouses, many of them renovated into coffee shops that keep the original feel — tiled floors, wooden doors and all. Khao Lak, a beachside resort town, has cafes where you can sit and look out over the Andaman Sea with nowhere you need to be. We've split them into two zones depending on the mood you're after.

blocks.text: Takua Pa Old Town cafes — sipping inside Sino-Portuguese shophouses

blocks.html: Takua Pa Old Town is easy to explore in half a day. There's street art along the walls telling the story of the tin-mining era, scattered with small cafes where the owners have renovated the old houses themselves. Most open late morning and close in the evening — a good place to duck out of the afternoon sun before carrying on with your photo walk.

items.name: Homeless Cafe
items.blurb: A cafe inside an old building renovated to keep the original structure throughout, with a raw, warm feel. They use dark-roast arabica beans that black-coffee drinkers love, and they stay open into the evening. It's the one Takua Pa locals recommend most often.

items.name: Seen Cafe at Takuapa
items.blurb: An old house renovated into a cafe with a little European-garden feel and plenty of photo corners. The standout sweets are the cheesecake and the lemon tart. Better suited to people who want to sit and take photos than to serious coffee drinkers.
items.meta: Soi Wat Khuan Tham, Udomthara Rd · Open 10:30–18:00 (closed Thu)

items.name: Mahamitr Cafe
items.blurb: A coffee shop that also does southern-Thai one-plate dishes. They use good-grade arabica beans, so it works if you want lunch and a coffee in one place. The atmosphere is calm and rarely crowded.

items.name: Mali Cafe
items.blurb: A homemade-bakes cafe with fresh baking every day; the cakes rotate with whatever's in season. The vibe is homey and sweet — a good stop for dessert with a coffee in the afternoon.
items.meta: Wattana Rd, Takua Pa subdistrict · Open 09:30–17:30

items.name: The Eighth Room Cafe
items.blurb: A coffee shop that takes its beans seriously, focused on medium roast with toast on the side, plated nicely. Good for anyone who wants to sit somewhere quiet and sip a proper coffee.
items.meta: Khuk Khak subdistrict, Takua Pa · Open 10:00–19:00 (Fri–Sun until 21:00)

items.name: OH LENG Takuapa
items.blurb: An old-town cafe that stays open later than the others on weekends. The atmosphere is easy-going — good for a group of friends settling in for a long chat.
items.meta: Takua Pa Old Town · Open Mon–Fri 10:00–18:00 · Sat–Sun until 20:00

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.html: Several Takua Pa cafes take a different weekday off (Tuesday, Thursday, or Friday). If there's a particular one you have your heart set on, check the shop's page before you set out — small cafes sometimes add extra closing days on their own.

blocks.text: Khao Lak Beachside Cafes — Sea Breeze and Sunset Views

blocks.html: Khao Lak is a resort town with a long stretch of beach, so the cafes here lean on the sea view and the Andaman sunset as their draw. Prices run a little higher than on the Takua Pa side because of the beachfront location, but the setting makes up for it.

items.name: Swell Cafe
items.blurb: A beachfront cafe on Khao Lak that's good for families, with a play zone for kids. You can sit indoors or out by the sand, with an open sea view. The drinks people go for are the cappuccino and the salted caramel.

items.name: Valhalla Khao Lak
items.blurb: A beachfront cafe with a wide view, best in the late afternoon while you wait for the golden light. It's a popular spot for people checking in and taking photos with the sea.

items.name: Garang Khaolak
items.blurb: A coffee shop and fresh bakery, with homemade ice cream as the standout. It's right on the main road, so it's an easy stop while you're driving around Khao Lak — good for a cool drink along the way.

items.name: Boonta by the Beach
items.blurb: A cafe right on Khao Lak Beach that keeps things simple, open midday to afternoon. You can sit and listen to the waves without the crowds — good for anyone who wants real quiet by the sea.

blocks.html: If you'd rather have a cafe surrounded by nature instead of right on the sea, the Khao Lak area also has a spot inside Khao Lak-Lam Ru National Park where you can sip a coffee among big trees. It opens on roughly official hours, around 09:30–16:30 — a good stop after a short forest walk.

items.name: Which side to pick
items.blurb: Want old shophouses, vintage photo corners, and lighter prices? Head to the Takua Pa side. Want sea views and a cool breeze, and you're willing to pay a bit more? Go for the Khao Lak side.

items.name: Best time to go
items.blurb: Takua Pa is best in the afternoon to escape the sun · Khao Lak is best in the late afternoon, waiting for the sunset over the sea.

faq.q: Where in Phang Nga can you find cafes to chill in all afternoon?
faq.a: They split into two zones. The Takua Pa Old Town side has cafes inside Sino-Portuguese shophouses, like Homeless Cafe and Seen Cafe, good for ducking out of the afternoon sun. The Khao Lak side has beachfront cafes like Swell Cafe and Valhalla, where you can sit in the breeze and wait for the sunset.

faq.q: Do cafes in Takua Pa and Khao Lak differ in price?
faq.a: The Takua Pa side is lighter on the wallet, with drinks around ฿55–110. The Khao Lak side, being beachfront cafes, runs up to about ฿80–150 for the beachside location — the trade-off being the sea view and the setting.

faq.q: What time do cafes in Takua Pa Old Town open?
faq.a: Most open late morning, around 09:30–10:30, and close in the evening. Some, like Homeless Cafe, stay open until 22:30, but many small cafes take a different weekday off, so it's worth checking the shop's page before you go.

faq.q: Is there a beachfront cafe in Khao Lak that works with kids?
faq.a: Yes — Swell Cafe on Khao Lak Beach has a play zone for kids and seating both indoors and out by the sand, so it suits families bringing young children.

faq.q: Can you do a Phang Nga cafe trip without your own car?
faq.a: The cafes are spread fairly far apart, especially between Takua Pa and Khao Lak, which are about 20 km apart. Renting a car or motorbike is the most flexible option. Within Takua Pa Old Town itself, though, you can walk between several of the cafes.
